title: Pay As You Go vs Subscription Card Fees: When Does It Pay?
description: A worked example comparing a 1.69% pay-as-you-go card rate with a £19-a-month plan at 0.99%: the break-even point and what to check before you switch.
h1: Pay as you go or subscription: when does a monthly plan pay off?
intro: Several card machine providers now offer a monthly subscription that lowers your transaction rate. Here’s how to work out whether it saves you money, using published figures.
keywords: pay as you go card machine
cardText: The break-even maths for monthly card fee plans.

sections.h2: The example: SumUp pay as you go vs Payments Plus
sections.html:
As published in October 2026, SumUp charges 1.69% on pay as you go with no monthly fee, or £19 a month for Payments Plus with a headline rate of 0.99%. The subscription saves 0.70% on eligible card takings, so the break-even point is:

Simple illustration using headline rates. Check which card types the 0.99% applies to, and whether online, keyed or international payments are charged differently.

sections.h2: Seasonal businesses: count your quiet months
sections.html: The subscription costs £19 even in months when takings are low. If you trade heavily in summer and barely at all in winter, total the year: an annual plan or switching between plans (if allowed) may change the answer.

Square and PayPal Point of Sale both publish 1.75% for in-person UK cards with no monthly fee. Square’s paid plans (from £29 a month) add software features rather than lowering the in-person card rate, so compare them on features. Above around £10,000 a month, SumUp and others offer custom pricing, and quoted contracts become worth exploring: see all providers.

1. Add up your last 12 months of card takings and divide by 12.
  2. Check your quietest month.
  3. Compare the yearly cost on each plan, including hardware.
  4. Get a quote from one or two contract providers if you’re above a few thousand pounds a month.
